question.text: The most suitable reagent for the conversion of <math> <mrow> <mtext>R</mtext> <mo>-</mo> <msub> <mtext>CH</mtext> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <mo>-</mo> <mtext>OH</mtext> <mo>→</mo> <mtext>R</mtext> <mo>-</mo> <mtext>CHO</mtext> </mrow> </math> is :

solution.text:
• KMnO4 will oxidize the alcohol to carboxylic acid.
• K2Cr2O7 will also make carboxylic acids.
• ​CrO3 in acetic acid is Jones reagent, it also converts alcohols to carboxylic acid.
•​ PCC is a weak oxidising agent. It limits the oxidation to the aldehyde.
